Nanchang Urban Rail Group Co..desc: A Nanchang city state-owned company that invests in, builds and operates the city's rail transit; its registered name is Nanchang Rail Transit Group Co., Ltd. (南昌轨道交通集团有限公司) and the Nanchang municipal state-asset commission holds 100% of it. A credit rating report filed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange gives registered and paid-in capital of RMB 2.615 billion and consolidated assets of RMB 72.5 billion at the end of March 2019.

sources.title: 联合资信 follow-up credit rating report on 南昌轨道交通集团有限公司 (corporate bond disclosure, Shanghai Stock Exchange)

Resettlement Research Center, Hohai Univ.desc: A research unit of Hohai University, a Chinese public university whose field is water resources. The university's own English listing of its research institutions carries a Research Center of Reservoir Resettlement Economics attached to the Ministry of Water Resources, and its School of Public Administration lists a resettlement (“Immigration”) research centre among 15 institutes.

sources.title: Hohai University, Scientific Research Institutions listing (en.hhu.edu.cn)
Hohai University, School of Public Administration — College introduction

State Council Leading Group Office for P.desc: A Chinese central government office in Beijing, set up in 1986, that ran the state's poverty reduction work. It ceased to exist on 25 February 2021, when its sign was taken down and the National Administration for Rural Revitalization was established at the same premises.

sources.title: 国家乡村振兴局正式挂牌 (Xinhua)

Open Shareholding Holding Company Barki.desc: Tajikistan's state power utility, registered with the Ministry of Justice on 3 June 1999 as Open Joint Stock Holding Company “Barqi Tojik”, whose sole shareholder is the Government of Tajikistan. Its audited accounts for 2018 give its principal activity as generation, transmission and distribution of electricity and thermal energy, five hydropower stations, and 11,230 employees at 31 December 2018.

sources.title: Barki Tajik entity audit report for the year ended 31 December 2018 (audited consolidated financial statements, Note 1)

Accra Metropolitan Assembly.desc: The metropolitan district assembly for Accra, Ghana. Its own pages give its legal basis as the Local Government Act, 1993 (Act 462), since amended as the Local Governance Act, 2016 (Act 936), with Legislative Instrument 2034, and describe a General Assembly at the apex with subordinate Sub-Metropolitan District Councils.

sources.title: Accra Metropolitan Assembly — The Assembly
Accra Metropolitan Assembly — History

Ministry of Local Government and Rural D.desc: Ghana's central ministry for local government, which makes policy for and oversees the country's Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies. In January 2025 it was merged, under Executive Instrument 1, with the Ministry of Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs and the sanitation ministry to form the Ministry of Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, which oversees 261 assemblies.

sources.title: Ministry of Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, Medium Term Development Plan 2026-2029 (National Development Planning Commission)

Direccion Provincial de Vialidad, Provin.desc: The road body of the Argentine province of Santa Fe, carried in the provincial budget as entity 601 “Vialidad” under jurisdiction 62, the Ministry of Public Works and Housing. It tenders works on provincial routes from its offices at Boulevard Muttis 880 in the city of Santa Fe and has its own Dirección General de Proyectos.

sources.title: Provincia de Santa Fe, programación de obras viales y de arquitectura (budget document naming Jurisdicción 62 - MOP y Vivienda, Entidad 601 - Vialidad)
Gobierno de Santa Fe, Licitación Pública N°32/2025 — Dirección Provincial de Vialidad

Direccion Nacional de Vialidad.desc: Argentina's national roads body, constituted as an autarchic entity by Decreto-Ley 505/58 and latterly operating within the Secretaría de Transporte of the Ministry of Economy. Decree 461/2025, signed 7 July 2025 and in force from its publication the next day, dissolved it and gave the study, construction, upkeep and improvement of the national trunk road network to the Ministry of Economy.

sources.title: Decreto 461/2025 (texto oficial, InfoLEG / argentina.gob.ar)

Pimpri Chinchwad Municipal Corporation.desc: A municipal corporation in the Indian state of Maharashtra, governed by the Maharashtra Municipal Corporation Act, 1949 and overseen by the state's Urban Development Department through the Director of Municipal Administration. India's Comptroller and Auditor General classes it as one of Maharashtra's three Category B corporations.

sources.title: Report of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India on Local Bodies, Government of Maharashtra — Chapter 3, Accounts and Finances of Urban Local Bodies

Hubli-Dharwad Bus Rapid Transit System C.desc: A state government company in Karnataka, India, listed by India's Comptroller and Auditor General as a working government company in the infrastructure sector under the name Hubli Dharwad BRTS Company Limited. Its last accounts finalised at the time of that report, for 2015-16, showed paid-up capital of ₹20 crore.

sources.title: Report No. 3 of 2018, Public Sector Undertakings, Government of Karnataka — Chapter 1, Functioning of State Public Sector Undertakings (CAG of India)
Report No. 3 of 2018, Public Sector Undertakings, Government of Karnataka — Appendices (CAG of India)

Tanzania National Roads Agency.desc: A Tanzanian government executive agency, constituted by order under the Executive Agencies Act and falling under the Ministry of Works and Transport, which oversees its performance on road maintenance. The national audit office records it as maintaining 12,176 km of trunk and 24,082 km of regional roads, and the Roads Act, 2007 requires it, as a roads authority, to prepare road maintenance programmes.

sources.title: Performance Audit Report on Maintenance of Roads, Controller and Auditor General, United Republic of Tanzania

Dar Rapid Transit Agency.desc: A Tanzanian government executive agency, established by Government Notice No. 120 of 2007 under the Executive Agencies Act No. 30 of 1997, as stated in its own tender notices.

sources.title: Tender notice issued by Dar Rapid Transit (DART) Agency, reciting its establishment instrument

Kenya National Highways Authority.desc: A Kenyan statutory body established under the Kenya Roads Act, 2007, which began operations in September 2008. It develops, rehabilitates and maintains the national trunk roads, which it gives as the Class S, A and B roads.

sources.title: Kenya National Highways Authority — About / Who we are

Kenya Urban Roads Authority.desc: A Kenyan state corporation established under the Kenya Roads Act, 2007, mandated to manage, develop, rehabilitate and maintain national trunk roads within urban areas. Its own page puts that network at about 4,625 km, paved and unpaved.

sources.title: Kenya Urban Roads Authority — Who we are

National Land Commission.desc: A Kenyan constitutional commission established under Article 67(1) of the 2010 Constitution and made operational by the National Land Commission Act, the Land Act and the Land Registration Act of 2012, its first commissioners taking office on 23 February 2013. Its functions include managing public land on behalf of the national and county governments and investigating land injustices and recommending redress.

sources.title: National Land Commission — Our History

Tanzania Airports Authority.desc: A Tanzanian executive agency, established on 29 November 1999 by Government Notice No. 404 of 1999 in relation to the Department of Aerodromes, under the Aerodromes (Licensing and Control) Act and the Executive Agencies Act. Its framework document gives its role as operating, managing, maintaining and developing government-owned airports, answering to the minister responsible for communications and transport.

sources.title: Executive Agencies (Tanzania Airports Authority) (Establishment) Order, 1999, G.N. No. 404 of 1999 (TanzLII)
